newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals quiet but weak.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals quiet but weak.

text.p: Precious metals prices balanced precariously on critical support levels on Thursday following a slump in prices this week, dealers and analysts said.
But early European trading was low key after prices drifted lower overnight on selling from gold producers, dealers said.
"Gold is sitting and doing nothing. It's the month-end which may be keeping things very quiet," a dealer said.
Gold fixed slightly lower at $379.30 an ounce, compared to $379.70 on Wednesday afternoon and a London close of $379.80/$380.30.
Gold has shed about $3.00 an ounce since the start of the week but was finding some support at the $379-$380 level, dealers said.
But prices could head to the next support level of $377.50 an ounce if recent selling pressure continued.
"Sentiment remains quite negative and technically it looks pretty bad, but up till now prices have remained within range," a dealer said.
The market's mood has soured since gold's attempted attempt to break out of a medium-term downtrend failed last week.
A lack of investor interest in precious metals and recent bearish talk of possible European central bank sales of gold reserves had further depressed the market, analysts said.
But some dealers dismissed such sales as an important near term factor, saying they had already been factored into the price.
The effect of reported gold sales by producers in South Africa and Australia were also sparking disparate views.
"There hasn't been a noticeable increase in producer selling. That's clear because we're still in the old price range," a dealer said.
Silver prices were barely changed from Wednesday's closing levels, down one cent at $4.81/$4.83.
On the downside, silver was eyeing support around $4.75 an ounce, which if breached would be followed by big losses towards $4.50, analysts said. Overhead, its big hurdle was $5.00.
Platinum and palladium were little changed from Wednesday's London close, hovering just above nearby support levels.
Platinum was indicated down $0.25 at $380.25/$381.25, while palladium was unchanged at $115.50/$116.50.
A break and close below the $380 support level would point to further losses towards the $375 support level for platinum.
Palladium was finding support around $115 an ounce, but a break lower would target $112 and then $110, dealers said.
